description: For each sex, count the distinct patients who have at least one examination.

a.request: Matching examinations to their patients, count the distinct examined patients (`Examination.ID`) for each `SEX` value (blank and missing sexes are their own groups) and work out each sex's share of the combined count. Among the sexes whose count is above the average count per sex, give one row with the total of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average amount by which their counts exceed that per-sex average.
a.sql:
WITH sex_counts AS (
  SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(DISTINCT e.ID) as count
  FROM Examination e
  JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
  GROUP BY p.SEX
),
total_info AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(count) as total_count,
    COUNT(*) as num_sexes,
    SUM(count) / COUNT(*) as avg_count_per_sex
  FROM sex_counts
),
sex_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    sc.SEX,
    sc.count,
    sc.count / ti.total_count as share,
    (sc.count - ti.avg_count_per_sex) as excess
  FROM sex_counts sc
  CROSS JOIN total_info ti
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT 
    SEX,
    count,
    share,
    excess
  FROM sex_shares
  WHERE count > (SELECT avg_count_per_sex FROM total_info)
)
SELECT 
  SUM(count) as total_counts,
  AVG(share) as avg_share,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess
FROM above_average

d.request: For each patient sex (including blank and missing values as separate groups), count the distinct patients who have at least one examination record, calculate each sex's share of the total examined patients, and for sexes above the per-sex average, provide a combined row with their aggregate patient count, average percentage share, and mean deviation above the per-sex average.
d.sql:
WITH examined_patients AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT e.ID, COALESCE(p.SEX, 'NULL') as Sex
  FROM Examination e
  JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
),
sex_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    Sex,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ID) as PatientCount,
    (COUNT(DISTINCT ID) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM examined_patients)) as PercentageShare
  FROM examined_patients
  GROUP BY Sex
),
avg_percentage AS (
  SELECT AVG(PercentageShare) as AvgPercentage FROM sex_stats
)
SELECT 
  Sex,
  PatientCount,
  PercentageShare,
  NULL as MeanDeviation
FROM sex_stats

UNION ALL

SELECT 
  'Above Average' as Sex,
  SUM(ss.PatientCount) as PatientCount,
  AVG(ss.PercentageShare) as PercentageShare,
  AVG(ss.PercentageShare - ap.AvgPercentage) as MeanDeviation
FROM sex_stats ss
CROSS JOIN avg_percentage ap
WHERE ss.PercentageShare > ap.AvgPercentage

b.request: For each patient sex (including blank and missing as separate groups), count the distinct patients who have at least one examination record, display the count and percentage share for each sex, and for sex groups with above-average examination frequency, provide a combined row with their aggregate patient count, mean percentage share, and mean distance above the per-sex average.
b.sql: WITH sex_groups AS (SELECT CASE WHEN p.SEX IS NULL THEN 'NULL' WHEN p.SEX = '' THEN 'BLANK' ELSE p.SEX END as sex_group, p.ID FROM Patient p INNER JOIN Examination e ON p.ID = e.ID), counts_by_sex AS (SELECT sex_group, COUNT(DISTINCT ID) as patient_count FROM sex_groups GROUP BY sex_group), total_patients AS (SELECT SUM(patient_count) as total FROM counts_by_sex), avg_count AS (SELECT AVG(CAST(patient_count AS FLOAT)) as avg_patients FROM counts_by_sex), stats AS (SELECT sex_group, patient_count, ROUND(100.0 * patient_count / (SELECT total FROM total_patients), 2) as percentage, (SELECT avg_patients FROM avg_count) as avg_patients FROM counts_by_sex), above_avg AS (SELECT sex_group, patient_count, percentage, CAST(patient_count AS FLOAT) - avg_patients as distance FROM stats WHERE patient_count > avg_patients) SELECT sex_group as sex, patient_count, percentage, NULL as mean_distance_above_avg FROM stats UNION ALL SELECT 'ABOVE_AVERAGE_COMBINED' as sex, SUM(patient_count) as patient_count, ROUND(AVG(percentage), 2) as percentage, ROUND(AVG(distance), 2) as mean_distance_above_avg FROM above_avg WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM above_avg) > 0 ORDER BY CASE WHEN sex = 'ABOVE_AVERAGE_COMBINED' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, patient_count DESC
b.raw: For each patient sex (including blank and missing as separate groups), count the distinct patients who have at least one examination record, display the count and percentage share for each sex, and for sex groups with above-average examination frequency, provide a combined row with their aggregate patient count, mean percentage share, and mean distance above the per-sex average.

c.request: Looking at the examination data by patient sex (blank and missing sexes as their own groups), how many were examined in each sex, and what share of the overall total is that? For the sexes above the per-sex average, give one row with their combined total, their average share, and on average how far above the per-sex average they are. For each sex, count the distinct patients who have at least one examination.
c.sql:
WITH sex_exams AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(p.SEX, 'Missing/Blank') as sex,
    COUNT(*) as exam_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) as distinct_patients
  FROM Examination e
  LEFT JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
  GROUP BY COALESCE(p.SEX, 'Missing/Blank')
),
totals AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(exam_count) as total_exams,
    COUNT(*) as num_sex_groups,
    SUM(exam_count) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) as avg_per_sex
  FROM sex_exams
),
with_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    se.sex,
    se.exam_count,
    se.distinct_patients,
    ROUND(se.exam_count * 100.0 / t.total_exams, 2) as share_percent,
    t.avg_per_sex,
    ROUND(se.exam_count - t.avg_per_sex, 2) as deviation_from_avg
  FROM sex_exams se, totals t
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT * FROM with_metrics WHERE exam_count > avg_per_sex
)
SELECT 
  sex,
  exam_count,
  share_percent,
  distinct_patients,
  deviation_from_avg
FROM with_metrics
UNION ALL
SELECT 
  'Above Average Combined',
  SUM(exam_count),
  ROUND(AVG(share_percent), 2),
  SUM(distinct_patients),
  ROUND(AVG(deviation_from_avg), 2)
FROM above_avg
